characters.name: Augustus
notes: ch1 [event] Lonesome Dove: Hot, dusty border town in the chaparral where the Hat Creek Cattle Company keeps its house, lots and the Dry Bean saloon nearby.
ch1 [event] Hat Creek: Nearly always-dry sandy creek by the outfit's wagon yard; a storm once washed the barn roof down it into the Rio Grande.
ch1 [event] Rio Grande: Border river beside the town; the outfit crosses it at night to raid Mexican stock, and cattle get chased back and forth across it.
ch1 [mention] Mexico: Lies across the river; Call bought his biting mare there, and the partners ride in to steal horses and cattle.
ch1 [mention] Pickles Gap: Tiny settlement founded by a lost Georgian; Call claims it has good shade, Augustus scorns it as even worse than Lonesome Dove.
ch1 [mention] Tennessee: Augustus, like the barber Dillard Brawley, is a Tennessean; whiskey makes him feel like a cool Tennessee morning.
ch1 [mention] Texas: Augustus thinks himself the only man in south Texas who can keep Call in proportion.
ch1 [mention] Prairie Dog Town Fork Red River: Where Comanches trapped Call, Augustus and six Rangers in dug holes; Augustus argued about coon dogs all night before they slipped away.
ch1 [mention] Scotland: Augustus reminds Call he was born there and brought over as a baby.
ch1 [end of chapter] with Call, Pea Eye, Newt, Bolivar at Lonesome Dove: at the Hat Creek Cattle Company house in town
ch2 [event] Lonesome Dove: Evening on the outfit's porch; piano music drifts from the Dry Bean saloon, where Lorena lives upstairs.
ch2 [mention] Fort Phantom Hill: Pea Eye recalls Call finding a large band of Indians near there in Ranger days.
ch2 [mention] Texas: Augustus's booming voice is famous across the state.
ch2 [mention] Virginia: Augustus spent a year at a college there and still boasts of his Greek and Latin.
ch2 [end of chapter] with Call, Pea Eye, Newt, Bolivar at Lonesome Dove: at their house; Augustus heading down to the Dry Bean saloon
ch3 [event] Lonesome Dove: Lorena lives above the Dry Bean saloon, cooking at first and then taking customers; Augustus offers her money just to talk.
ch3 [mention] San Francisco: Lorena's dream destination because it sounds cool; Augustus claims to have been and describes the bay at length.
ch3 [mention] Canada: Augustus jokes they could live there just as cheaply as in this heat.
ch3 [end of chapter] with Lorena at Lonesome Dove: in Lorena's room above the Dry Bean saloon, heading down to play cards
ch4 [event] Lonesome Dove: Augustus walks past the Pumphreys' store to the Dry Bean, plays cards late, and lends Dish two dollars before the cowboy heads up to Lorena.
ch4 [event] Hat Creek: Augustus pauses on its dry sandy bed to buckle on his pistol on the way into town.
ch4 [mention] Tennessee: Augustus compares its misty nights to dry border nights and remembers card games with his sisters there.
ch4 [mention] Texas: Xavier came believing it a land of opportunity; cowhands argue whether Augustus or Shanghai Pierce is louder.
ch4 [mention] Philadelphia: Lippy's hat bears a Philadelphia maker's label, which he takes as proof of quality.
ch4 [mention] St. Louis: Lippy grew up there and wishes he could go back.
ch4 [end of chapter] with nobody at Lonesome Dove: back at the outfit's house
ch5 [event] Lonesome Dove: Augustus bakes biscuits at sunrise; over breakfast Call floats a trail drive and offers Dish work, then spots Deets riding in with Jake Spoon.
ch5 [mention] Rio Grande: Sunrise lights the flats along it; Dish imagines taking Lorena for a buggy ride beside it.
ch5 [mention] Mexico: Call plans to ride down that night to gather stock, possibly enough for a herd to drive north.
ch5 [mention] Pickles Gap: Augustus mocks Call's herd idea by suggesting they drive it there.
ch5 [end of chapter] with Call, Newt, Pea Eye, Bolivar, Dish Boggett at Lonesome Dove: on the back porch of the outfit's house
ch6 [event] Lonesome Dove: Jake Spoon rides in after ten years away, eats breakfast, pitches a Montana drive and admits a killing; Newt recalls Jake visiting his late mother here.
ch6 [mention] Arkansas: Jake has ridden hard all the way from there, fleeing trouble.
ch6 [mention] Montana: Jake praises its rich grass and urges a cattle drive there before others arrive, once the Indians are subdued.
ch6 [mention] Wichita country: Where Pea Eye once missed a wolf and his bullet killed Call's horse beyond a hill.
ch6 [end of chapter] with Call, Newt, Pea Eye, Deets, Bolivar, Dish Boggett at Lonesome Dove: at the outfit's house and lots; Dish, Pea and Newt digging the well
ch7 [event] Lonesome Dove: Jake and Augustus drink by the springhouse until Jake naps; at the corrals Call breaks the mare and surprises Augustus by proposing a drive north.
ch7 [event] Hat Creek: Augustus walks down its dry bed past the corrals and the new well.
ch7 [mention] Brazos River: Rangers found Deets's heavy sheepskin coat in a deserted cabin there; Jake dreaded crossings; Call recalls camping there with Black Beaver.
ch7 [mention] Fort Phantom Hill: Augustus links the coat's discovery to a fight near there.
ch7 [mention] San Antonio: One of Jake's trail towns; Clara was at school there during the 1856 raid; the outfit's bank account is kept there.
ch7 [mention] Ogallala: Jake glimpsed Clara outside a store there, with her husband Bob, and only tipped his hat.
ch7 [mention] Nebraska: Clara and Bob Allen live there; Augustus imagines it a hard life.
ch7 [mention] North Platte River: Clara's family lives on it, Bob trading horses to the Army; Augustus realizes a Montana drive must cross the Platte near her.
ch7 [mention] Austin: Clara ran her parents' store there after an 1856 Indian raid killed them.
ch7 [mention] Vicksburg: A toeless acquaintance named Harwell later died there in the war.
ch7 [mention] Washington, D.C.: Augustus jokes the pursuing sheriff might get lost and end up there.
ch7 [mention] Mexico: The partners have prospered modestly by bringing Mexican cattle across to sell to traders.
ch7 [mention] Rio Grande: The outfit crosses here to gather stock; Black Beaver once boasted of knowing all the country between the Columbia and this river.
ch7 [mention] Texas: As Rangers they guarded its settlers; the Governor kept their troop on the border during the war.
ch7 [mention] Brush Country: Filled with cowboys and traders once the postwar cattle market began, ending the partners' rangering.
ch7 [mention] Kansas: South Texas ranchers trail herds north to its railheads.
ch7 [mention] Pecos River: They sometimes talked of rangering beyond it, but Apache country had too few settlers to need Rangers.
ch7 [mention] Montana: Call proposes driving a herd there; Augustus calls it wilderness but warms to it.
ch7 [mention] Powder River: Augustus jokingly proposes meeting Call there with a herd.
ch7 [mention] Georgia: Augustus jokes that without Rangers the bankers would still be back there eating greens.
ch7 [end of chapter] with Call, Dish Boggett, Bolivar, Deets at Lonesome Dove: at the outfit's corrals and well
ch9 [event] Lonesome Dove: Call promises Wilbarger forty horses by sunup; Newt is finally given a pistol and the outfit saddles up at sundown.
ch9 [event] Hat Creek: Drunk Dish retches in its sandy bed while Jake and Augustus look on amused and Call arrives to judge him.
ch9 [event] Rio Grande: At dusk the seven-man outfit crosses it heading into Mexico; it was once just a river inside the hacienda's lands.
ch9 [event] Mexico: The outfit rides into it at nightfall to raid horses.
ch9 [mention] Hacienda Flores: Pedro Flores's huge Coahuila ranch, holding hundreds of horses, many with Texas brands; Call targets it for a hundred-horse raid.
ch9 [mention] Coahuila: Mexican state where the Hacienda Flores is the largest ranch; its old lands once spread into Texas.
ch9 [mention] Montana: Call wants extra horses as a remuda for a drive there; Augustus resists the cold.
ch9 [mention] Yale College: Wilbarger claims he studied Latin there; Augustus doubts it.
ch9 [end of chapter] with Call, Jake Spoon, Deets, Pea Eye, Newt, Dish Boggett at Rio Grande: just crossed into Mexico at dusk, riding southeast toward the Hacienda Flores about thirty miles off
ch10 [event] Rio Grande: The outfit crosses it and trots southeast by moonlight; Newt keeps track only by knowing the river lies to his left.
ch10 [event] Mexico: Newt's first night raid there; the dark empty brush country holds wild longhorns that bolt from the riders.
ch10 [event] Hacienda Flores: The riders skirt an out camp and the big camp; Augustus calls it northern Mexico's best-armed ranch; the outfit splits to take the horse herd.
ch10 [mention] Mexico City: Augustus mocks Call's caution, saying they needn't detour by way of Mexico City.
ch10 [end of chapter] with Jake Spoon, Pea Eye, Dish Boggett at Hacienda Flores: sent to take the Flores horse herd, south of the big camp
ch11 [event] Hacienda Flores: The outfit finds a small herd of stolen Wilbarger horses, then Call, Pea and Newt run off a hundred-plus Flores horses past the sleeping hacienda.
ch11 [event] Mexico: Jake grumbles about riding across it; Newt fears that horse stealing there could get him hanged.
ch11 [mention] Texas: The captured horses are mostly Texas stock; Newt notes horse stealing is a hanging crime on the Texas side.
ch11 [mention] Galveston: Where the two lost Irishmen had been trying to go.
ch11 [mention] Ireland: Augustus jokes about how far off course travellers from there have strayed.
ch11 [mention] Montana: Call plans to take surplus horses there; Newt tries to imagine its buffalo, mountains and snow.
ch11 [mention] Arkansas: Augustus teases that Jake is used to its whores and feather pillows.
ch11 [end of chapter] with nobody at Hacienda Flores: rode off with two horses to fetch the stranded Irishmen and follow the herd home
ch12 [event] Lonesome Dove: At the corrals Wilbarger cuts out his horses and offers thirty-eight for Call's mare; Augustus arrives with the Irishmen, who find the dusty town a letdown.
ch12 [event] Sabinas: Augustus says he detoured there overnight with the Irishmen, visiting its brothel and taking saddles and nags from drunk bandits.
ch12 [mention] Rio Grande: Call tells Augustus to move the stolen horses upriver; Pea recalls the Rangers once going up the river after bandits.
ch12 [mention] Rainey ranch: Call may go there to hire some of Maude Rainey's many sons; Augustus once courted Maude.
ch12 [mention] United States: Sean is disappointed that America is hot sand and thornbrush, with no snow.
ch12 [mention] Montana: Call says the outfit is driving there; Wilbarger warns it is too far, cold, bear-ridden and maybe Indian-held.
ch12 [end of chapter] with Pea Eye, Newt, Deets, Dish Boggett, Bolivar at Lonesome Dove: at the Hat Creek house after breakfast; Augustus is to move the horse herd upriver that afternoon
ch14 [event] Lonesome Dove: Jake joins Augustus drinking on the porch; Augustus teaches the Irishmen to ride and shoot at a cactus; the prime horses are sent back to town to be penned.
ch14 [event] Rio Grande: The stolen herd grazes near it; Augustus looks across expecting Pedro Flores at dusk and moves the poorer horses upriver.
ch14 [mention] Mexico: Augustus tells Jake to keep the herd from straying back into it; Jake says Gus has caused him more trouble than all its bandits.
ch14 [mention] Sabinas: Augustus had no time there to adjust the Irishmen's stirrups.
ch14 [mention] Montana: Call is hiring cowboys for the drive there; Jake regrets suggesting it and fears scalping.
ch14 [mention] San Francisco: Jake worries Lorie will hold him to taking her there; Augustus teases him about it.
ch14 [mention] California: Jake idly talks of drifting off there with Lorena.

ch14 [end of chapter] with Pea Eye, Jake Spoon, Newt, Allen O'Brien, Sean O'Brien at Rio Grande: moving about a hundred poorer horses north and upriver from near Lonesome Dove at dusk, watching for Pedro Flores
ch16 [event] Lonesome Dove: Call returns to find Augustus napping on the porch; Augustus reports that Pedro Flores has reportedly died, which leaves Call unexpectedly hollow.
ch16 [mention] Mexico: Pedro Flores long dominated about a hundred miles of border; Augustus jokes they could take over northern Mexico now.
ch16 [mention] Montana: Call tells the Raineys Jake praises it; after hearing of Pedro's death Call says they might as well go.
ch16 [mention] Republican River: Augustus says he might drown in it like the Pumphrey boy did.
ch16 [end of chapter] with Call at Lonesome Dove: Augustus on the Hat Creek porch; Call riding off in town to find and hire Jasper Fant
ch17 [event] Lonesome Dove: Jake lives with Lorena above the Dry Bean while new hands play cards there; on a hot day Augustus wins a cut of cards and buys Lorena's favors.
ch17 [mention] Hat Creek cow camp: The outfit has been gathering and branding cattle for about ten days; Call has put Jake to work there.
ch17 [mention] San Francisco: Lorena means to hold Jake to his promise to take her there; Augustus doubts Jake will follow through.
ch17 [mention] Arkansas: Lorena cites the man Jake killed there; Augustus calls it a stray shot that hit a dentist.
ch17 [end of chapter] with Lorena, Lippy at Lonesome Dove: in Lorena's room and the saloon at the Dry Bean
ch18 [event] Hat Creek cow camp: Brush camp where the herd is held and branded; Bolivar's snake stew upsets Jasper; Jake declines the drive and Augustus suggests bringing Lorie.
ch18 [mention] Lonesome Dove: Augustus spent the day there; Jake leaves camp to ride back to it.
ch18 [mention] San Antonio: Jake says he may stay there instead; Augustus doubts Lorie wants to go back where she came from.
ch18 [mention] San Francisco: Augustus reports Lorie is eager to go there.
ch18 [mention] Montana: Jake, who called it a cowman's paradise, now balks at the drive; Call hopes to start north Monday.
ch18 [mention] Denver: Augustus suggests stopping there; Jake wishes he had gone there rather than Fort Smith.
ch18 [end of chapter] with Bolivar, Newt, Allen O'Brien, Sean O'Brien, Jasper Fant, Bill Spettle at Hat Creek cow camp: holding the herd in a valley near the river about five miles from town
ch19 [event] Hat Creek cow camp: Newt night-herds and dreams of the north; cowboys gamble future wages by the fire; Deets, uneasy about the hasty drive, builds branding fires with Newt and Pea.
ch19 [mention] Great Plains: Newt imagines its endless grass, buffalo, elk and bears; Deets recalls water holes drying fast there in summer.
ch19 [mention] Ogallala: Augustus says the young hands must wait for it, rumored to be a sinful town.

ch19 [end of chapter] with Newt, Deets, Pea Eye, Sean O'Brien, Needle Nelson, Bert Borum, Jasper Fant, Dish Boggett at Hat Creek cow camp: building branding fires and holding the herd near the river about five miles from Lonesome Dove; drive due to start within days
ch20 [mention] Montana: Jake complains his friends expect him to help drive cattle there just because he mentioned it.
ch22 [event] Hat Creek herd camp near Lonesome Dove: Jake and Lorena, in pants, ride in at supper and stun the hands; Jake says they'll travel alongside toward Denver; Call decides to start tomorrow.

ch22 [end of chapter] with Call, Bolivar, Newt, Pea Eye, Dish Boggett, Needle Nelson, Allen O'Brien, Sean O'Brien, Jasper Fant at Hat Creek herd camp near Lonesome Dove: at the cook fire beside the gathered herd, about to start north
ch23 [event] Hat Creek herd camp near Lonesome Dove: At dawn Soupy Jones arrives and is hired; Gus's pigs turn up; Augustus hitches the mule wagon while Call culls the remuda.
ch23 [event] Jake and Lorena's camp near Lonesome Dove: Augustus finds Lorena burning breakfast and Jake nursing a mesquite thorn in his swollen thumb amid a scattered camp.
ch23 [event] Lonesome Dove: Augustus pries his sign off the corral fence, consoles a despairing Xavier, and leaves with Lippy, who signs on to the drive.
ch23 [mention] Powder River: Augustus teases that most of the hands will drown before reaching it.
ch23 [mention] Republican River: Augustus warns Lippy he might drown in it.
ch23 [mention] Alabama: Augustus thinks of Lorena as a young prostitute from there.
ch23 [mention] San Francisco: Augustus thinks Lorena's resolve may get her there; Xavier says he would have taken her.
ch23 [mention] San Antonio: Augustus suggests Xavier go there to recruit a new prostitute.
ch23 [mention] Texas: Augustus drank there against the heat and feels lucky to be leaving it alive.
ch23 [mention] Montana: Augustus expects to drink against the cold there; tells Lippy that's where he's headed.
ch23 [end of chapter] with Lippy at Lonesome Dove: in the wagon, just leaving town across the chaparral flats toward the herd
ch24 [event] Hat Creek herd camp near Lonesome Dove: Hands ready gear in the heat; Lippy is put over the horses; Call culls stock with Deets, names him scout, and keeps a mottled little bull.
ch24 [mention] Montana: Call wants bulls for stocking it; Augustus jokes Call could end up its governor passing laws against cattle thieves.
ch24 [mention] Canada: Augustus tells Ben Rainey it is the land of the northern lights.
ch24 [mention] Lonesome Dove: Augustus asks if Call isn't sorry to leave the place they pacified, and wonders how Xavier will manage.

ch24 [end of chapter] with Call, Deets, Newt, Pea Eye, Dish Boggett, Lippy, Bolivar, Needle Nelson, Bert Borum, Ben Rainey, Jasper Fant, Soupy Jones at Hat Creek herd camp near Lonesome Dove: about to start the herd north once the day's heat eases

ch25 [event] First day's trail north of Lonesome Dove: The herd of about 2,600 sets out in choking dust; Newt nearly loses strays; Call and Gus watch from a knoll as Deets returns to lead them to bed-ground.
ch25 [mention] Lonesome Dove: Seen in the distance from the hill; Augustus feels a whiskey might make him sentimental about it, Call does not.
ch25 [mention] Rio Grande: Augustus marks leaving the river they patrolled so long and wants a speech; it is still visible behind them.
ch25 [mention] Mexico: Visible beyond the river from the knoll as the drive begins.
ch25 [mention] Brush Country: A dense mesquite belt between them and San Antonio; Call asks whether to go through it, Gus says go through.
ch25 [mention] Texas Gulf Coast: The mosquito-ridden alternative route around the brush that Augustus rejects.
ch25 [mention] Brazos River: Augustus doubts the rickety wagon will last that far.
ch25 [mention] Arkansas: Augustus says thorn-pricked Jake wished he'd stayed there and accepted his hanging.
ch25 [end of chapter] with nobody at First day's trail north of Lonesome Dove: lingering alone on a knoll watching the sunset and herd
ch30 [end of chapter] with Call at Nueces River: herd some distance back, south of the Nueces, its dust visible behind Jake and Lorena
ch31 [event] Stampede ground south of the Nueces: A night sandstorm then lightning and drenching rain stampede the herd into mesquite thickets; Newt ends lost and soaked, plodding on Mouse.
ch31 [end of chapter] with Call, Bolivar at Stampede ground south of the Nueces: wagon stopped in the brush several miles south of the Nueces when the storm struck
ch33 [mention] San Antonio: Dish jokes the missing Gus has gone there for a shave.
ch33 [end of chapter] with nobody at Stampede ground south of the Nueces: missing; last seen just after dawn riding east
ch34 [event] Nueces River: Drying out at their north-bank camp, Lorena gets her mare back from Gus; Jake slaps her for refusing San Antonio; Gus swims back across.
ch34 [mention] San Antonio: Jake wants to gamble there a week; Lorena refuses to go back; Gus warns any lawman would search there first.
ch34 [mention] Lonesome Dove: Gus says the runaway mare was heading home there when he found her.
ch34 [end of chapter] with nobody at Nueces River: swam back to the south side, riding through the brush to rejoin the herd
ch35 [event] Nueces River: The herd crosses a little downriver through mosquito swarms; Sean rides into a nest of water moccasins and dies, buried under a live oak near the north bank.
ch35 [mention] Montana: Destination of the drive; Augustus closes the burial by telling everyone to go on there.
ch35 [mention] Ogallala: Augustus teases Dish about its women and muses he might stop there to settle near Clara.
ch35 [mention] Nebraska: Augustus remarks it is a long way off.
ch35 [mention] Kentucky: Home of the horse trader Clara chose to marry.
ch35 [mention] Austin: Augustus recalls Clara telling him of her marriage outside her little store there some sixteen years ago.
ch35 [mention] Yellowstone River: Augustus jokes he wishes they were already there.

ch35 [end of chapter] with Call, Deets, Newt, Pea Eye, Dish Boggett, Allen O'Brien, Jasper Fant, Bolivar, Lippy, Needle Nelson, Soupy Jones, Bert Borum at Nueces River: just across the Nueces, moving on north from Sean's grave
ch39 [event] San Antonio River: The jittery crew dreads moccasins, but Deets finds a shallow crossing a mile or two from camp and the herd, wagon and pigs cross without trouble.
ch39 [mention] Montana: Augustus asks who will buy the cattle there; Call says the point is claiming land before settlers arrive.

ch39 [end of chapter] with Call, Deets, Pea Eye, Newt, Dish Boggett, Jasper Fant, Allen O'Brien, Soupy Jones, Bert Borum, Bolivar, Lippy at San Antonio River: just across the San Antonio River, about a week after the Nueces crossing
ch41 [event] Wagon-wreck creek near San Antonio: Bolivar's accidental shotgun blast stampedes the mules; the wagon flips off a cutbank onto Lippy, who survives, and Bol quits and heads home.
ch41 [mention] Montana: Augustus tells Bol he can rejoin them there if he changes his mind.
ch41 [end of chapter] with Call, Newt, Pea Eye, Lippy, Dish Boggett, Jimmy Rainey, Bill Spettle at Wagon-wreck creek near San Antonio: at the creek with a broken wagon, short of passing San Antonio

ch42 [event] San Antonio: Call and Gus buy a wagon and mules north of the river; at the Buckhorn saloon Gus bloodies a rude bartender, sheriff Tobe vouches for them, and they leave past the neglected Alamo.
ch42 [event] Settlements south of San Antonio: Two tiny new hamlets with a church and a few stores prompt Augustus to complain that settlement is ruining the country.
ch42 [mention] Tennessee: Augustus says had he wanted civilization he would have stayed there writing poetry.
ch42 [mention] New Orleans: Augustus jokes San Antonio may rival it if it keeps growing.
ch42 [mention] Canadian River: The Rangers once chased Kicking Wolf's band all the way to it, earning brief fame and a photograph.
ch42 [mention] Mobile: Hometown of John, the hot-tempered new Buckhorn owner.
ch42 [mention] Montana: Tobe wistfully says he might have joined the drive there if not married.
ch42 [mention] Texas: When they first came in the Forties, everyone still talked of Travis and the Alamo.
ch42 [end of chapter] with Call at San Antonio: leaving town at night with a new wagon, heading back to the herd
ch44 [event] Hat Creek herd camp west of Austin: Country opens into better grass; the cookless crew grumbles over Augustus's scrambled eggs while Call rides off alone each night.
ch44 [event] Clara's orchard: Augustus detours to a live-oak grove by a spring-fed pool where he and Clara picnicked, and weeps remembering her refusal of his proposal.
ch44 [event] Lorena's camp by the limestone bluff: Bruised Lorena waits alone by a pool; Jake left in anger two days ago, so Augustus stays to keep her company.
ch44 [mention] Austin: Call rides on alone to hire a cook and buy horsehair reins; Jake has evidently gone there to gamble.
ch44 [mention] High Plains: As Rangers there, Augustus's keen eyes told sage bushes from Indians in the mirages.
ch44 [mention] Pecos River: Another Ranger haunt where Augustus's eyesight proved itself.
ch44 [mention] Kentucky: Home of the horse trader Clara married instead of Augustus.
ch44 [end of chapter] with Lorena at Lorena's camp by the limestone bluff: west of Austin, three miles from Clara's orchard
ch45 [event] Lorena's camp: Lorena waits here for Jake; Augustus swims in the cold water hole, Blue Duck rides in to water his horse, threatens, then leaves.
ch45 [mention] Hat Creek outfit's cow camp: Augustus urges Lorena to come stay at the drive's camp after Blue Duck appears; she refuses because the men stare.
ch45 [mention] Lonesome Dove: Lorena considers riding back there; she recalls feeling the same every day while living there.
ch45 [mention] San Francisco: Lorena's dream destination, which she hears is cool; Augustus warns that life there is still just life.
ch45 [mention] California: Lorena realizes Jake will not take her there and proposes Augustus go with her instead.
ch45 [mention] Canadian River: Blue Duck threatens to mutilate Augustus if he ever comes north of it.
ch45 [mention] Red River: Blue Duck's Comancheros used to raid settlers along it, killing adults and stealing horses and children.
ch45 [mention] New Mexico: Western end of the range Blue Duck's gang raided.
ch45 [mention] Arkansas: Eastern end of the range Blue Duck's gang raided.
ch45 [mention] Ogallala: Augustus says he is headed there, to a woman named Clara, rather than to California.
ch45 [mention] Nebraska: Where Ogallala lies; Lorena scorns Augustus travelling that far for a woman.
ch45 [mention] Denver: Augustus promises Lorena a train ticket to California if they both reach it.
ch45 [mention] Texas: Lorena fears she will never leave it; Augustus says they are halfway out already.
ch45 [mention] Fort Worth: Augustus says Texas does not extend much north of it.
ch45 [mention] Galveston: Augustus has heard of Blue Duck killing there and guesses he may be heading that way.
ch45 [end of chapter] with nobody at Lorena's camp: riding back toward the cow camp from Lorena's pool
ch46 [event] Hat Creek outfit's cow camp: Call returns from town without the new cook; hearing of Blue Duck he posts Deets as guard and spends the night on a nearby bluff watching the herd.
ch46 [event] Lorena's camp: Newt is sent from the drags to guard Lorena there overnight until Jake returns.
ch46 [mention] Town where Call hired a cook: Call hired a Mexican cook there and heard Jake's name mentioned in saloons but did not find him.
ch46 [mention] Lonesome Dove: Maggie lived and died there in a room above a saloon; Call and Augustus argue whether it is a place worth living.
ch46 [mention] Texas: Augustus mocks the Texas Rangers Call led as half-outlaws who obey him blindly.
ch46 [end of chapter] with Pea Eye, Dish Boggett, Needle Nelson at Hat Creek outfit's cow camp: herd bedded in a little valley under a full moon
ch47 [event] Hat Creek outfit's cow camp: The herd stampedes at night toward the bluffs; at dawn Pea finds Newt afoot and the new cook Po Campo walks in with his donkey.
ch47 [mention] Lonesome Dove: Newt longs for the biscuits Augustus baked there before leaving his ovens behind.
ch47 [end of chapter] with Call, Pea Eye at Hat Creek outfit's cow camp: herd regathered after a night stampede
ch48 [event] Hat Creek outfit's cow camp: Po Campo wins the crew with plover-egg omelet and fried grasshoppers; Jake arrives saying Lorena is gone, and Augustus rides off alone after Blue Duck.
ch48 [mention] Lorena's camp: Jake returns to find the camp gear left but Lorena and both animals gone; Augustus concludes Blue Duck took her.
ch48 [mention] Canadian River: Augustus repeats Blue Duck's threat about coming north of it.
ch48 [mention] Mexico: Augustus guesses Po Campo's wife lives there; the cook says she is in hell instead.
ch48 [end of chapter] with nobody at Hat Creek outfit's cow camp: rode off alone at night to track Blue Duck and recover Lorena
ch54 [mention] Blanco River: Where a bungling horsethief once rustled stock before Augustus and Call caught and hanged him some twelve years back.
ch54 [mention] Llano Estacado: By the second day Augustus judges Blue Duck is heading for this vast tableland.
ch54 [event] Palo Duro Canyon: Blue Duck used to retreat beyond it; Augustus recalls giving up a waterless chase there with Call, then rides to its edge now.
ch54 [mention] San Antonio: Augustus once warned Call that killing their horses on the plains would mean a long walk back there.
ch54 [event] Clear Fork Brazos River: Augustus crosses it and passes an abandoned half-built cabin, a reminder of settlers driven off by Comanche raids.
ch54 [event] Brazos River: Augustus camps cold on a bluff in the post-oak country near it; years ago he and Call shot it out with Aus Frank in a thicket there.
ch54 [mention] Trinity River: Frontier settlers came up it and the Brazos in the Fifties, only to retreat from Comanche terror.
ch54 [mention] Lonesome Dove: Augustus misses its familiar noises in the silent plains; the partners once doubted buffalo-slaughter reports there.
ch54 [event] Wichita River: After finding Lorena's dead mare and leaving the scrub, Augustus crosses it and bears west.
ch54 [mention] Adobe Walls: Abandoned Bent trading post on the Canadian where buffalo hunters gather; Augustus suspects Blue Duck took Lorena there and heads for it.
ch54 [event] Canadian River: Augustus finds old Aus Frank piling huge pyramids of buffalo bones beside it, spends the night, then rides east along it.
ch54 [event] Comanche captive crossing on the Canadian: Old Comanche captive-trading crossing; Augustus inspects it, finding many horse tracks but not Blue Duck's.
ch54 [mention] Valley of Tears: Notorious spot near the captive crossing where Comancheros split up captive mothers and children for sale.
ch54 [event] Quitaque: Parched country of shallow red canyons, dust devils and mirages that Augustus rides through toward the Palo Duro.
ch54 [event] Prairie Dog Town Fork Red River: Augustus crosses it amid many prairie dogs on his way west.
ch54 [mention] Texas: Talk there held that the raiding bands were scattered, which Augustus now doubts.
ch54 [mention] Waco: Aus Frank kept a store there, robbed the bank beside it, was caught by Augustus and Call, and broke jail.
ch54 [mention] Montana: Augustus asks the ex-trapper whether he reached it; no answer.
ch54 [event] High Plains: Empty, buffalo-stripped plains with a road of bones; Augustus recalls once riding beside the vast southern herd here.
ch54 [end of chapter] with nobody at Canadian River: riding east along the Canadian at dawn from Aus Frank's bone camp toward Adobe Walls

ch30 [end of chapter] with Augustus at Nueces River: herd some distance back, south of the Nueces, its dust visible behind Jake and Lorena

ch35 [mention] Montana: Destination of the drive; Augustus closes the burial by telling everyone to go on there.

ch42 [mention] Washington, D.C.: Call scoffs that a thousand Comanches together could have taken it.

ch44 [mention] Guadalupe River: The little creek at Clara's orchard drains into it.
ch44 [event] Lorena's camp by the limestone bluff: Bruised Lorena waits alone by a pool; Jake left in anger two days ago, so Augustus stays to keep her company.

characters.name: Newt
notes: ch1 [event] Lonesome Dove: Hot, dusty border town in the chaparral where the Hat Creek Cattle Company keeps its house, lots and the Dry Bean saloon nearby.

ch1 [end of chapter] with Augustus, Call, Pea Eye, Bolivar at Lonesome Dove: at the Hat Creek Cattle Company house in town

ch2 [end of chapter] with Augustus, Call, Pea Eye, Bolivar at Lonesome Dove: at their house; Augustus heading down to the Dry Bean saloon

ch5 [mention] Dodge City: Newt admires Dish for having trailed cattle there more than once.
ch5 [end of chapter] with Augustus, Call, Pea Eye, Bolivar, Dish Boggett at Lonesome Dove: on the back porch of the outfit's house

ch13 [end of chapter] with Lippy, Xavier Wanz at Lonesome Dove: at the Dry Bean saloon, waiting for Jake to come back

ch15 [end of chapter] with Xavier Wanz, Lippy at Lonesome Dove: playing cards in the Dry Bean saloon

ch17 [mention] San Francisco: Lorena means to hold Jake to his promise to take her there; Augustus doubts Jake will follow through.
ch17 [mention] San Antonio: Needle Nelson comes from north of it; Lorena considers ordering new dresses from there.
ch17 [mention] Arkansas: Lorena cites the man Jake killed there; Augustus calls it a stray shot that hit a dentist.
ch17 [end of chapter] with Augustus, Lippy at Lonesome Dove: in Lorena's room and the saloon at the Dry Bean

ch20 [mention] San Francisco: Lorena insists Jake keep his promise to take her there.
ch20 [mention] San Antonio: Jake suggests going there to gamble; Lorena refuses because Tinkersley once took her there.
ch20 [mention] Denver: Jake talks of reaching it and then crossing over to San Francisco.
ch20 [end of chapter] with Jake Spoon at Lonesome Dove: in Lorena's room above the Dry Bean saloon

ch21 [mention] San Francisco: Lorena tells Xavier they are bound there; Jake thinks her beauty could attract rich men there; Xavier predicts she'll never arrive.

ch21 [mention] Arkansas: Jake already has trouble there over a shooting.
ch21 [mention] Baton Rouge: Lorena's father died there; Xavier's look reminds her of his.
ch21 [end of chapter] with nobody at Lonesome Dove: in her room above the Dry Bean, planning to leave in the afternoon

ch22 [end of chapter] with Jake Spoon at Hat Creek herd camp near Lonesome Dove: riding off to make their own camp on a ridge near the herd
ch23 [event] Jake and Lorena's camp near Lonesome Dove: Augustus finds Lorena burning breakfast and Jake nursing a mesquite thorn in his swollen thumb amid a scattered camp.

ch23 [mention] San Francisco: Augustus thinks Lorena's resolve may get her there; Xavier says he would have taken her.
ch23 [end of chapter] with Jake Spoon at Jake and Lorena's camp near Lonesome Dove: about to pack and leave their camp half a mile from the herd

ch30 [mention] San Francisco: Lorena knows reaching it means many more river crossings and briefly calls the dream foolish.
ch30 [end of chapter] with Jake Spoon at Nueces River: camped under a big mesquite on the north bank, bracing for a storm from the south

ch32 [end of chapter] with Jake Spoon at Nueces River: huddled under a tarp beneath the north bank during the storm; Lorena's mare has run off

ch34 [mention] Lonesome Dove: Gus says the runaway mare was heading home there when he found her.
ch34 [end of chapter] with Jake Spoon at Nueces River: packing up camp on the north bank, disagreeing over going to San Antonio

ch40 [event] San Antonio: Lorena refuses to go in, angering Jake; he rides to town alone at night for whiskey and races back.
ch40 [mention] Lonesome Dove: Lorena's mare no longer looks back toward it; Jake wishes he had left Lorena there.
ch40 [end of chapter] with Jake Spoon at Jake and Lorena's camp near San Antonio: camped a mile from the herd, about an hour from San Antonio

ch44 [end of chapter] with Augustus at Lorena's camp by the limestone bluff: west of Austin, three miles from Clara's orchard

ch45 [mention] Lonesome Dove: Lorena considers riding back there; she recalls feeling the same every day while living there.
ch45 [mention] San Francisco: Lorena's dream destination, which she hears is cool; Augustus warns that life there is still just life.
ch45 [mention] California: Lorena realizes Jake will not take her there and proposes Augustus go with her instead.
ch45 [mention] Alabama: Lorena's sickly brother stayed there with their grandmother.
ch45 [mention] Ogallala: Augustus says he is headed there, to a woman named Clara, rather than to California.
ch45 [mention] Nebraska: Where Ogallala lies; Lorena scorns Augustus travelling that far for a woman.
ch45 [mention] Denver: Augustus promises Lorena a train ticket to California if they both reach it.
ch45 [mention] Texas: Lorena fears she will never leave it; Augustus says they are halfway out already.
ch45 [end of chapter] with nobody at Lorena's camp: alone at the pool, still waiting for Jake, near the drive's cow camp
ch46 [end of chapter] with Newt at Lorena's camp: Newt sent to guard Lorena about a mile from the herd

ch47 [end of chapter] with nobody at Lorena's camp: alone, waiting for Jake

ch49 [event] Hat Creek outfit's cow camp: Blue Duck rides with his captive straight through the stampeding herd without being seen.

ch49 [mention] San Francisco: Lorena despairs of ever seeing it.
ch49 [end of chapter] with Blue Duck, Ermoke at Grassland beyond the sand river: a short ride past a broad red-sand river, several days from the herd, waiting for moonrise

ch55 [mention] Lonesome Dove: Lorena recalls hiding her words there but finding them readily when Jake arrived.
ch55 [end of chapter] with Monkey John, Dog Face at Blue Duck's camp on the Canadian: camp on the Canadian River plains near a creek

ch57 [end of chapter] with Augustus at Blue Duck's camp on the Canadian: at the outlaw camp near the Canadian; Lorena too weak to travel fast

ch58 [event] Canadian River: Treeless river where the camp lies; July later rides across it into the breaks to the north.
ch58 [end of chapter] with Augustus at Canadian River: riding east from the burial site looking for shade, planning to wait for Call and the herd

ch4 [mention] Matamoros: Dish delivered horses there and lost a month's pay gambling before riding about a hundred miles upriver.
ch4 [mention] Abilene: Trail town where Dish imagines buying Lorena a present.
ch4 [mention] Dodge City: Dish usually brings back ribbons and combs from there for Mexican girls.
ch4 [end of chapter] with Lorena, Lippy, Xavier Wanz at Lonesome Dove: at the Dry Bean saloon; Dish upstairs with Lorena, about to leave with a trail outfit next week

ch5 [mention] Mexico: Call plans to ride down that night to gather stock, possibly enough for a herd to drive north.
ch5 [mention] Dodge City: Newt admires Dish for having trailed cattle there more than once.

ch5 [end of chapter] with Augustus, Call, Newt, Pea Eye, Bolivar at Lonesome Dove: on the back porch of the outfit's house

ch7 [end of chapter] with Call, Augustus, Bolivar, Deets at Lonesome Dove: at the outfit's corrals and well
ch8 [event] Lonesome Dove: Wilbarger rides in seeking horses past Augustus's elaborate livery sign; Dish finds Lorena now taken with Jake at the Dry Bean and drinks heavily.
ch8 [event] Rio Grande: Call lopes the mare about twenty miles along it; heartsick Dish sits by it for an hour watching a coyote.
ch8 [mention] Mexico: Call announces a night raid there; Newt hopes to be taken along; the raider Cortinas is a hero south of the river.

ch8 [mention] Matagorda: Dish considers riding back there and abandoning the outfit.
ch8 [end of chapter] with Jake Spoon, Lorena, Lippy, Xavier Wanz at Lonesome Dove: drinking at the Dry Bean saloon
ch9 [event] Lonesome Dove: Call promises Wilbarger forty horses by sunup; Newt is finally given a pistol and the outfit saddles up at sundown.
ch9 [event] Hat Creek: Drunk Dish retches in its sandy bed while Jake and Augustus look on amused and Call arrives to judge him.
ch9 [event] Rio Grande: At dusk the seven-man outfit crosses it heading into Mexico; it was once just a river inside the hacienda's lands.
ch9 [event] Mexico: The outfit rides into it at nightfall to raid horses.
ch9 [end of chapter] with Call, Augustus, Jake Spoon, Deets, Pea Eye, Newt at Rio Grande: just crossed into Mexico at dusk, riding southeast toward the Hacienda Flores about thirty miles off

ch11 [end of chapter] with Jake Spoon, Deets at Mexico: driving about forty recovered Wilbarger horses back toward Lonesome Dove; position at dawn not stated

ch12 [mention] Matagorda: Dish grew up there and boasts of its knee-high grass.
ch12 [end of chapter] with Augustus, Pea Eye, Newt, Deets, Bolivar at Lonesome Dove: at the Hat Creek house after breakfast; Augustus is to move the horse herd upriver that afternoon

ch15 [mention] Rio Grande: Jasper Fant is a cowboy from upriver.
ch15 [mention] Texas: Xavier notes Mexican women are plentiful across south Texas; Jasper jokes Mexicans could retake Texas with the Captain away.
ch15 [end of chapter] with Deets, Jasper Fant at Lonesome Dove: Deets by the water trough in the Hat Creek corral; Dish and Jasper riding back to the pens from the saloon

ch17 [end of chapter] with Call, Jake Spoon, Jasper Fant, Needle Nelson, Bert Borum at Hat Creek cow camp: gathering and branding cattle near Lonesome Dove ahead of the drive

ch18 [end of chapter] with Call, Needle Nelson, Bert Borum, Pea Eye, Deets at Rio Grande: riding from the cow camp to the river to cross into Mexico for a last drag of cattle

ch52 [event] Gully where Roscoe was robbed: In a thunderstorm the outlaws Hutto and Jim strip and rob Roscoe; Janey pelts them with rocks until July arrives and captures them.
ch52 [event] Fort Worth: July delivers the outlaws to the sheriff, tells Roscoe in a saloon he will hunt Elmira first, and boards Janey at a livery stable.
ch52 [event] July's camp north of Fort Worth: Camped amid trail herds; by morning Janey has followed them on foot and returns July's boarding money.
ch52 [end of chapter] with July Johnson, Roscoe Brown, Joe at July's camp north of Fort Worth: heading north onto the plains, a day or more beyond Fort Worth, searching for Elmira
ch56 [event] Canadian River: The party rides to the steep-banked river, spots a campfire downstream, camps upriver at a canyon mouth, and Augustus and July ride toward the fire.
ch56 [event] July's canyon-mouth camp on the Canadian: Where a canyon slopes into the riverbed; Roscoe and the youngsters are left here while the two men ride off.
ch56 [end of chapter] with Roscoe Brown, Joe at July's canyon-mouth camp on the Canadian: waiting at a canyon mouth on the Canadian, several miles upriver from the outlaw camp
ch58 [event] July's canyon-mouth camp on the Canadian: A big night intruder kills Roscoe, Janey and Joe; July returns to find them, and he and Augustus bury them under rocks on the plain above.
ch58 [event] Canadian River: Treeless river where the camp lies; July later rides across it into the breaks to the north.

characters.name: Blue Duck
notes: ch45 [event] Lorena's camp: Lorena waits here for Jake; Augustus swims in the cold water hole, Blue Duck rides in to water his horse, threatens, then leaves.
ch45 [mention] Canadian River: Blue Duck threatens to mutilate Augustus if he ever comes north of it.
ch45 [end of chapter] with nobody at Lorena's camp: rode off over a ridge from the pool; destination unknown
ch49 [event] Lorena's camp: Blue Duck slips in at night, ties Lorena to her saddle and leads her away.
ch49 [event] Hat Creek outfit's cow camp: Blue Duck rides with his captive straight through the stampeding herd without being seen.
ch49 [event] Blue Duck's route through empty hill country: Several days of hard riding through empty rocky ridges, crossing many creeks, while horses give out and Lorena suffers thirst.
ch49 [event] Stream where Blue Duck rested: After a full night and day riding, they stop here until dark; Lorena finally drinks and Blue Duck threatens her.
ch49 [event] Red-sand river crossing: Wide riverbed of boggy reddish sand with a thin brown stream; Ermoke and three renegades wait on the far side.
ch49 [event] Grassland beyond the sand river: Past the river the party stops at sundown and Ermoke's men assault Lorena before riding on by moonlight.
ch49 [end of chapter] with Lorena, Ermoke at Grassland beyond the sand river: a short ride past a broad red-sand river, several days from the herd, waiting for moonrise
ch55 [event] Blue Duck's camp on the Canadian: Lorena is held and abused in a filthy camp near a creek; Blue Duck kills a young Kiowa while gambling and sends Ermoke to ambush Gus.
ch55 [event] Canadian River: The men complain they are stranded on it without horses; Blue Duck expects Gus to come down it.
ch55 [mention] Quitaque: Blue Duck says his pursuer wandered off across it before figuring out the trail.
ch55 [end of chapter] with nobody at Canadian River: rode off from the camp at dawn, destination unstated
ch57 [event] Blue Duck's camp on the Canadian: Blue Duck abandons Lorena to the Kiowas, who mutilate the dying Dog Face; Augustus and July charge in and Augustus kills the whole gang.
ch57 [event] Canadian River: Blue Duck rides off toward it; Augustus warns that a dangerous man is loose along it.
ch57 [end of chapter] with nobody at Canadian River: rode off from the camp toward the river, whereabouts unknown

characters.name: Po Campo
notes: ch47 [event] Hat Creek outfit's cow camp: The herd stampedes at night toward the bluffs; at dawn Pea finds Newt afoot and the new cook Po Campo walks in with his donkey.
ch47 [end of chapter] with Newt at Hat Creek outfit's cow camp: walking the last few hundred yards to the wagon
ch48 [event] Hat Creek outfit's cow camp: Po Campo wins the crew with plover-egg omelet and fried grasshoppers; Jake arrives saying Lorena is gone, and Augustus rides off alone after Blue Duck.
ch48 [mention] Mexico: Augustus guesses Po Campo's wife lives there; the cook says she is in hell instead.

ch48 [end of chapter] with Call, Pea Eye, Newt, Deets, Dish Boggett, Jasper Fant, Lippy, Allen O'Brien, Soupy Jones, Needle Nelson at Hat Creek outfit's cow camp: herd moving north; a day passes with no sign of Augustus or Jake
ch59 [event] Fort Worth: The herd camps west of town; most of the crew go carousing and find Jake gambling and snubbing them, then return badly hungover.
ch59 [mention] Llano Estacado: Po Campo once raised sheep there until Blue Duck killed his three sons; Call recalls its unnerving emptiness and fears Gus has vanished there.

ch59 [end of chapter] with Call, Pea Eye, Deets, Newt, Dish Boggett, Jasper Fant, Needle Nelson, Soupy Jones, Bert Borum, Allen O'Brien, Ben Rainey at Fort Worth: herd moving north from its camp west of Fort Worth toward the Red River
ch60 [event] Treeless plain south of the Red River: Heavy rain catches the herd two days short of the Red; the crew spends a sodden night on horseback.
ch60 [event] Indian Territory: The herd grazes on wet grass north of the Red; the crew camps there with Irish and Spanish songs while Call camps apart.

ch60 [end of chapter] with Call, Pea Eye, Deets, Newt, Dish Boggett, Jasper Fant, Needle Nelson, Soupy Jones, Bert Borum, Allen O'Brien at Indian Territory: camped just north of the Red River crossing
